claude_proposed_widenings.name: alter_appearance
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Disguise Self makes the caster look different — clothing, armor, weapons, and body — for a timed duration. No v4 effect atom covers visual appearance modification of a creature. The closest existing atom (alter_item_kind) is scoped to items, not creatures. A new effect atom is needed to represent illusion-based appearance changes with their implicit constraint (same limb arrangement; fails physical inspection).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You make yourself—including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings on your person—look different until the spell ends.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: OngoingOperation.alter_appearance
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The ongoing_effect family needs a new OngoingOperation variant that carries the alter_appearance atom. The two existing variants (roll_modifier, damage_on_hit) do not model any form of visual state change on the attachment target.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: You can seem 1 foot shorter or taller and can appear heavier or lighter. You must adopt a form that has the same basic arrangement of limbs as you have.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: alter_appearance.piercing_check
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The spell includes a detection mechanic: a creature can take the Study action and succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against the caster's spell save DC to see through the disguise. The existing ability_check resolution atom exists in v4, but the surface needs a sub-field on the alter_appearance operation (or a rider type) to encode this 'pierce-the-illusion' check as part of the effect's grammar.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: To discern that you are disguised, a creature must take the Study action to inspect your appearance and succeed on an Intelligence (Investigation) check against your spell save DC.
